caption:
🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Thursday, 29 October 2026

1. 💷 Chancellor Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax
Chancellor John Healey has unveiled £100 for energy bills and a tax on banks in his first Budget. He says the measures target the cost of living, but opposition parties say he has not been bold enough.

2. 💼 Tax thresholds frozen for three more years
The point at which people start paying income tax, and the point at which they move into the higher rate, have been frozen for three more years.

3. 📈 National minimum wage to rise after Budget announcement
Chancellor John Healey has announced an increase in the national minimum wage. It will mean a pay rise for around 2.3 million workers across the UK.

4. 📊 Official statistics on visa holder earnings and employment published
The statistics cover visa holders' earnings, employment and income tax for the year ending March 2026. They match Home Office visa records with HMRC PAYE Real Time Information data and include main applicants and dependants.

5. 🎓 Two-year graduate visa to be allowed at 'high-compliance' universities
The government also announced an expansion of the 'high potential individual' visa route to the top 150 global institutions, as part of efforts to attract 'the world's best graduates'.

6. 🚫 Scotland bans sale of nicotine products to under-18s
Scotland has banned the sale of nicotine products to under-18s. The ban forms part of the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026.

7. ⚽ Russo becomes England's leading scorer in Women's Champions League
Alessia Russo scored a hat-trick in Arsenal's 3-0 win over Benfica. It made her England's all-time leading goalscorer in the Women's Champions League.

8. 👑 King Charles shows off dance moves during Caribbean tour
King Charles showed off his dance moves on the second day of his Caribbean tour. Earlier in the day, he paid his respects to the island's fallen servicemen and women.

Sources: BBC, Evening Standard, GOV.UK Home Office, The Independent, BBC Sport. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay.
